title: introduce-heuristic-seeder-and-tenant-warmstart-templates
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Motivation: onboarding tenant workloads with safe, cost-aware defaults is still noisy — teams often need to tune batching/caching/quant profiles by hand. This PR adds an automated 'heuristic seeder' that generates tenant-level starter templates (batching, cache TTLs, quantization tier hints) based on a short workload fingerprint and historical econ signals. The goal is to reduce first-week unit-econ regressions and shorten ramp time for Dedicated/Private customers.

What this PR does: adds a new service (econ/seeder) that ingests a compact workload fingerprint (qps, avg prompt tokens, 95th latency, percent streaming, distribution of seq lengths) and emits a recommended template with: preferred batch size ranges, prefix-KV caching policy, quantization baseline (int8/4/none) with safety margins, and a conservative prefill policy for cold starts. Templates are expressed as YAML and can be applied via the existing tenant-templates API or exported as 'templates-as-code' for infra teams.

Key implementation notes: the seeder is intentionally heuristic-first (no ML training loop) to keep outputs explainable for audits. It encodes rules from the econ playbook: prefer smaller batches (< 8) when p95 latency budget <= 120ms; enable KV prefix caching for workloads with >20% repeated prefixes; prefer int8 for seq <1024 and QPS > 5k unless quality-locked. Safety gates are enforced: each template includes a rollback profile and a dry-run score estimator that simulates token-cost delta against the current tenant baseline.

Files/areas: services/econ/seeder.py, infra/cli/cost-templates.py, docs/heuristic-seeder.md, tests/unit/test_seeder.py, charts/templates/values.yaml.

Checklist: [x] implement seeder service core rules; [x] CLI export/apply flow; [x] unit tests and integration smoke; [x] docs and template examples; [x] add telemetry events for decisions.

Related: references ENG-2145 (tenant warmstart), ENG-2210 (cost-defaults initiative). This is a follow-up to prior cost-default PR work but introduces an opinionated seeder rather than only recommending UI suggestions. Expect follow-up work to add a lightweight learnable ranking layer (post-v1) and a canary rollouter.

review_thread: Samir Patel (reviewer) commented on 2025-11-13: Can we add telemetry IDs to each decision branch for downstream attribution? I want to be able to track which heuristic produced the template.
Ava Martinez (author) replied on 2025-11-13: Yes — added decision_event tags to the seeder output and instrumented the main paths. See services/econ/seeder.py:decision_event constants.

Riley O'Connor (reviewer) commented on 2025-11-15: The safety rollback profile looks good, but we should guarantee that the dry-run estimator runs in <200ms for interactive use. Unit tests show ~180ms on CI but please add a microbenchmark and a timeout in the CLI.

Ava Martinez (author) replied on 2025-11-16: Added microbenchmark harness and CLI timeout (infra/cli/cost-templates.py). Estimator optimized by memoizing token-length cost model — now consistently <120ms in our lightweight bench.
Jun Park (reviewer) commented on 2025-11-18: Could the seeder recommend quantization = int4 for some cold PDFs? Risky — suggest we scope to int8 for v1 and keep int4 as opt-in.
Ava Martinez (author) replied on 2025-11-18: Agreed. v1 only emits int8 or none and marks int4 candidates in the template as 'experimental' with explicit opt-in flag.
release_notes: Added heuristic seeder to generate tenant cost-default templates (batching, caching, quantization hints). Introduces CLI commands 'cost-templates export|apply' and new telemetry for seed decisions. Safe-by-default: rollback profiles and dry-run estimator included.
notes_for_operators: Operators: the seeder emits templates to /templates/service with a TTL of 30d. To opt out for a tenant, POST {"opt_out_seeder": true} to /admin/tenant/settings. When importing via CLI, use --dry-run to preview token-cost delta.
